disclosures.text: Metric formulas and denominators: every ratio has its numerator, denominator, value and status in the table that reports it; ratio names are defined in metrics.METRIC_DEFINITIONS (definitions.json 'metrics'); wide-table columns are defined in definitions.json 'tables'. Undefined ratios stay undefined (empty value, status undefined_empty_denominator), never 0.

Pass 1 precedence and Pass 2 eligibility: Pass 1 claims rows first; Pass 2 only claims rows Pass 1 left; everything else abstains. Final Pass 1 and Pass 2 never overlap by construction. For the RF Router this is verified from the artifacts (Pass 1 score equivalence); for GLASS it is code-level only (no per-fold rule sets).

Positive leakage: Pass 1 actual positives (routed NOT_SUBSCRIBE) / all positives (pass1_leakage_share); within-band leakage is Pass 1 positives / Pass 1 rows (pass1_positive_rate); Pass 1 NPV is Pass 1 negatives / Pass 1 rows.

Frozen reference flags: lr.in_stage_f2_cv (LR calibrated probability >= its stored threshold, selected on ALL training labels: in-selection, rates optimistic) and ebm.nested_f2 (stored fold-nested EBM raw-score decisions). Both come from the GLASS arm and are the common reference for both routers; the RF Router's own black-box cascade uses other upstream models.

Overall (frozen) comparisons keep each side's own flag rate on all rows; matched-rate comparisons re-cut LR / EBM at each arm's Pass 2 count K per fold on the common eligible population, label-free. K is the router's observed count (a descriptive control, not a pre-registration); the two arms have different K.
EBM raw scores are never pooled or ranked across folds (their fold-specific nested thresholds show the scales differ): EBM strata, ranks and threshold positions are within the router outer fold.

LR calibrated probabilities are isotonic, so large tied blocks occur. Strata keep tied scores in one bin (merged edges). Matched selections break ties at the K-th score by a predetermined label-free rule (ascending SHA-256 of the row's index label (label-free, fixed per row; not row order)) and report strict / inclusive bounds.

Two kinds of expected positives: calibrated model expectations (sums of LR or EBM calibrated OOF probabilities; assume the calibration is right) and internal standardisation (expected_stratified_*: the group's rows' (fold, stratum) positive rates on the same labels). Neither is a null distribution or a test.
Cells with fewer than 30 rows are flagged low_support and excluded from within-stratum contrasts (difference left empty).

Final-state Pass 1 / Pass 2 overlap is available and zero by construction (a routing invariant, not evidence of independent signals). Pre-routing signal overlap is unavailable: GLASS candidate-rule matches and per-fold rule sets, and RF Pass 2 outer scores, were never persisted. The full-train GLASS rule set is not applied to training rows (in-sample).

Shared component, code-level only: crossfit_stage2 defaults to glass_rf_model='fold_rf', passing each outer fold's RF to the GLASS fit (segment prioritisation by its feature_importances_); that fold forest's oof_proba is the RF Router's Pass 1 score. The artifacts' own record of glass_rf_model is not read.
Pass 2 fit-time populations differ historically: GLASS 'full', RF 'oof_remainder' (F17, Commit 3). Pass 2 differences are not attributable to the selector alone.

Commit 4 defines the successor; PR 38 applies it.

Historical test-set exposure: the held-out test split was evaluated in PRs 33-36, and the October 23 artifacts store test metrics and test-oracle thresholds. PR 37 diagnostics read only allowlisted training-side fields and prevent further test-derived influence; they do not make the test split untouched. No test label, test prediction or test-derived threshold is read or exported here.

No claim of Stage 3 / Stage 4 or integrated-cascade benefit, no independent external validation, no ranking of the routers, no significance test. Fold values are descriptive, not independent replicates; no standard errors are given.

Known limitation (identified after Step 2D; definitions unchanged): the 3 x 3 joint grid splits each score at within-fold tertiles, so its top cell contains rows on both sides of both reference thresholds. For populations defined by those thresholds (reference-flag groups and 'unique vs' groups), expected_stratified_lr_x_ebm compares them with rows across the threshold and is not interpretable; use the calibrated expectations. Decile expectations share the bias to a smaller degree.

Known limitation (identified after Step 2D; definitions unchanged): pooled ('all') stratum rows sum bin k of every fold, and where LR isotonic ties merge decile edges the bin indices shift, so pooled LR bin k covers different score ranges in different folds (LR occupied bins by fold: fold 0: 9, fold 1: 8, fold 2: 8, fold 3: 10, fold 4: 9; merged in folds [0, 1, 2, 4]). Pooled LR strata and LR-conditioned pooled contrasts are approximate; per-fold cells and all expectations are unaffected; the EBM strata are aligned.

The artifacts do not record the code that produced them. MANIFEST.json 'code' identifies the diagnostic and export code at generation (LF-normalised SHA-256), not the router implementations; router identity is the artifacts' own record (MANIFEST.json 'routers').

2A.compare_state_distributions: Historical test-set exposure: the held-out test split was evaluated in PRs 33-36, and the October 23 artifacts store test metrics and test-oracle thresholds. PR 37 diagnostics read only allowlisted training-side fields and prevent further test-derived influence; they do not make the test split untouched.

Observational comparison of the historical outer OOF routes on the same 32,950 training rows and 5 outer folds. Coverage and abstention describe how much each router decides, not how well: abstained rows continue to Stages 3-4, and a router state is not the cascade's final outcome. No ranking is implied and no significance test is made; per-fold values come from models fitted on overlapping training sets and are not independent replicates.

Pass 2 fit-time populations differ: GLASS 'full' (normalised 'full'); RF 'OOF Pass 1 remainder (RF router design)' (normalised 'oof_remainder'). At decision time both routers let Pass 2 claim only rows Pass 1 left; the difference is the rows Pass 2 was fitted and selected on (Commit 3, F17), so Pass 2 differences are not attributable to the rule selector or forest alone.

RF Router thresholds were tuned against constraints derived from the GLASS Router's historical pooled OOF metrics (constraint_source='match_glass_oof'). The arms are not independent, and because those pooled metrics include each outer fold's own rows, the RF Router's outer-fold thresholds depend weakly on that fold's labels. Independent shared criteria are Commit 4's.

Not recorded in the historical artifacts, so no score-level or rule-level comparison is made: GLASS Router: feature_hash (no feature-matrix hash is stored); GLASS Router: fold_rule_sets (per-fold GLASS rule sets and candidate rules are not persisted); GLASS Router: fold_summaries (GLASS cross-fit fold summaries are not persisted); RF Router: feature_hash (no feature-matrix hash is stored); RF Router: pass2_outer_scores (RF Pass 2 outer out-of-fold scores are not persisted); RF Router: pass1_outer_scores (RF Pass 1 outer scores are not stored in the router artifact; see check_rf_pass1_score_equivalence).

These observed distributions describe the historical routers. They must not be used to choose the Commit 4 operating-contract criteria, which are to be declared independently of both arms' observed performance.

Reference lr.in_stage_f2_cv: Stage 1 LR operating point (threshold_source in_stage_f2_cv, 0.10 in the Oct 23 artifact). In-selection: the threshold was chosen on the labels of the same training rows it is applied to; rates computed with it are optimistic.
Reference ebm.nested_f2: Stage 3 EBM fold-nested operating point: each fold's raw-space threshold was selected on inner OOF scores of that fold's training rows.

An intercepted reference false positive (Pass 1 & flag & negative) is a potential benefit; a suppressed reference true positive (Pass 1 & flag & positive) is an error. Both are reported with their own denominators and are never netted.

These are overlaps on the same training rows, not the integrated cascade's performance: Stage 4 combines router and upstream evidence, so a reference flag inside Pass 1 is not necessarily removed from the final output. 'Retained' counts and retained_upstream_precision describe a hypothetical Pass 1 veto of the reference flags.

Common reference: both routers are measured against the same flags, the GLASS arm's Stage 1 LR and Stage 3 EBM at their registered primary operating points. The RF Router's own black-box cascade uses other upstream models; this is not that cascade.

Fold plans: lr (lr.in_stage_f2_cv): 10 folds, not the routers' 5; router-fold values group this reference's out-of-fold flags by the routers' partition; ebm (ebm.nested_f2): same as the routers' outer folds. Fold-level rows use the routers' outer folds; per-fold values are descriptive, not independent replicates, and no significance test is made.

Matched flag rate on the common eligible population (16,189 rows neither router routed to Pass 1; a shared decision-time population, not either router's fit-time Pass 2 population). It excludes 74 GLASS Pass 2 rows that RF routed to Pass 1 and 813 RF Pass 2 rows that GLASS routed to Pass 1; frozen results on all rows are reported separately.

Selection: within each router outer fold, the reference's K highest-scoring common-eligible rows, K = that arm's Pass 2 rows in the fold's common population. No label is read. Ties at the K-th score: ascending SHA-256 of the row's index label (label-free, fixed per row; not row order); the strict / inclusive cuts (operating_points.matched_rate_cut) bound the tie effect and neither is preferred.

K is the router's observed count: a descriptive operating-rate control, not an independent pre-registration and not evidence of superiority. The matched LR / EBM flags are re-cut at each router's rate; they are not the frozen operating points or a configuration either model was tuned for.

Arm-specific: GLASS and RF have different K, so each arm is compared with its own matched references; this is not an equal-flag-count comparison between the routers. lr_or_ebm_matched is the union of two K-matched sets and its size is not matched.

Scores: LR calibrated_probability (out-of-fold over 10 folds; calibration isotonic, nested per fold); rows of one router fold come from several LR fold models and are compared in the calibrated space. EBM raw_model_score, ranked only within its own fold (EBM shares the routers' outer folds; its fold-specific nested thresholds show raw scores are not comparable across folds). GLASS / RF Pass 2 are never ranked or truncated.

2D.overlap_notes: Q1 (functional behaviour) is answered descriptively from final routing states. Q2 (incremental information) is only described here: score-conditional rates and expectations are not a controlled test, and nothing here measures Stage 4 or the integrated cascade.

Final Pass 1 and Pass 2 never overlap by construction (Pass 1 precedence). Zero final overlap is a routing invariant, not evidence of independent signals; candidate / signal overlap is unavailable because no per-row candidate matches, fold rule sets or RF Pass 2 outer scores were persisted.

Score strata were fixed before any result was inspected: within each router outer fold, 10 label-free quantile bins of the LR calibrated probability and of the EBM raw score, and a 3 x 3 LR x EBM grid; merged duplicate edges keep tied scores together; cells under 30 rows are low-support; the threshold band is +/- 0.05 in within-fold percentile.

Expected positives are descriptive. expected_lr_calibrated / expected_ebm_calibrated assume the calibrated OOF probabilities are right; expected_stratified_* use the same labels inside each (fold, stratum) cell (internal standardisation). Neither is a null distribution, and no standard error is given because rows, folds and model decisions are not independent.
Conditioning on one score at a time does not establish information beyond both; the joint grid is coarse, so within-cell variation remains possible.
Unique = relative to the stated reference or to the other router, as labelled. Agreement is not inherently better and disagreement is not inherently complementary.
Common reference: the GLASS arm's Stage 1 LR (threshold selected on all training labels; rates optimistic) and Stage 3 EBM (fold-nested raw thresholds) for both routers.
Pass 2 fit-time populations differ (GLASS 'full', RF 'oof_remainder'; Commit 3, F17).
